title: 1966 AHSME Problem 38
statement: In triangle \(ABC\) the medians \(AM\) and \(CN\) to sides \(BC\) and \(AB,\) respectively, intersect in point \(O.\) \(P\) is the midpoint of side \(AC,\) and \(MP\) intersects \(CN\) in \(Q.\) If the area of triangle \(OMQ\) is \(n,\) then the area of triangle \(ABC\) is:

solutions.text:
Area ratios are affine-invariant, so take \(A=(0,0),\) \(B=(2,0),\) and \(C=(0,2).\) Then \[ \begin{gathered} M=(1,1),\\ O=(\frac{2}{3},\frac{2}{3}),\\ P=(0,1). \end{gathered} \] Line \(MP\) is \(y=1,\) and it meets median \(CN\) at \(Q=(\frac{1}{2},1).\) Thus \([OMQ]=\frac{1}{12},\) while \([ABC]=2.\) Their ratio is \(24,\) so \([ABC]=24n.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: Find \(M,O,P,Q\) and compare the two areas
